text:
alex: Heads up — terraform plan on platform-staging is proposing to replace the kubernetes_secret 'app/credentials' even though I imported that secret yesterday via kubectl. Not sure why plan thinks it needs to recreate.

alex: plan snippet:
```
-/+ kubernetes_secret.app_credentials (replace)
  id: "app/credentials" => "1048576"
  data: "(sensitive)" => "(sensitive)"
  metadata {
    annotations {
      managed-by = "terraform"
    }
    name = "credentials"
    namespace = "app"
  }
```

jordan: did you run `terraform state show kubernetes_secret.app_credentials`? sometimes import created an id that doesn't match the provider format. also what provider version?

alex: running that now, output looks weird — id shows `app/credentials` but when I imported I did `terraform import kubernetes_secret.app_credentials app/credentials` (kubectl import pattern). provider is kubernetes v2.16.0.

maria: two possibilities — provider expects `namespaces/NAME/secrets/NAME` style id depending on provider version, or the live resource has extra fields (ownerRefs/metadata.resourceVersion) that terraform diffs as change. did you `terraform refresh` after import?

alex: did `terraform refresh` — it updated state but plan still wants replace.

jordan: can you paste `terraform state show` output (redact data)? might show computed / generated fields that terraform manages.

alex: output:
```
# kubernetes_secret.app_credentials:
resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_credentials" {
  id = "app/credentials"
  metadata {
    annotations = {
      "managed-by" = "kubectl"
      "some-other" = "val"
    }
    name = "credentials"
    namespace = "app"
  }
}
```

maria: aha — annotation `managed-by` is `kubectl` in state/live diff. your tf config expects `terraform`. that will cause a diff but should be a minor change, not replace — unless other fields differ. check for `immutable` or `type` changes on secret or if it's referenced by a volumeClaim that forces recreate.

tim: also check the k8s provider `server_side_apply` / `force_replace_on_change` settings — some clusters treat certain secret updates as requiring replace. what does plan say about dependent resources?

alex: plan shows a dependent replace for a deployment that mounts the secret as envFrom. error in logs during dry-run: `error: secret data changed, recreating pod` not k8s api replace but terraform decides to recreate to update computed fields.

sre-bot: notice: there is a stale state lock on backend from run 1766999900 by ci-runner-4. lock TTL expired but not cleaned. run `terraform force-unlock 8a7b6c` if you confirm no running applies.

jordan: do NOT force-unlock if CI apply is still active. check `terraform operations list` or your CI job status. if safe, `terraform force-unlock 8a7b6c` then `terraform refresh`.

alex: CI job finished an hour ago, looks safe. I'll force-unlock and try a `terraform refresh -target=kubernetes_secret.app_credentials` then re-plan.

maria: alternative quick fix: if you only care about annotations, patch the live secret to match terraform's expected annotation, then `terraform refresh` so the diff disappears:
```
kubectl -n app patch secret credentials -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"managed-by":"terraform"}}}'
terraform refresh -target=kubernetes_secret.app_credentials
terraform plan
```

jordan: if import id format is the issue, you can `terraform state mv` to the expected id or re-import with the provider-specific id. check `terraform import` docs for the kubernetes provider.

alex: ran the patch + refresh — plan now shows only an in-place update for annotations, no replace. thanks all. I'll run apply in ~10m from my laptop.

tim: nice. once applied, consider adding an explicit `metadata.annotations` block in tf config to avoid drift. also add a note in the runbook about import id formats.

alex: will do. thanks :thumbsup:
